description: The Africa GeoPortal is an ArcGIS Online organisation and hub run by Esri for discovering, using and sharing geographic content about Africa, including its people, infrastructure and environment. Contents: on 29 September 2026 its search API listed 859 datasets, mixing Esri Living Atlas layers (land cover 2050 scenarios, terrestrial ecosystems, lithology, biomass carbon), OpenStreetMap extracts for Africa (highways, waterways, buildings, medical and educational facilities, points of interest), GRID3 layers (settlement extents, Nigeria roads and energy substations), IWMI distance rasters and national layers shared by agencies, such as Senegal's high-voltage power lines and airports. Country sub-portals (Angola, Botswana, Eswatini and others) filter the same content; the Angola portal showed 32 items, Botswana 9 and Eswatini none. Coverage: the African continent, uneven by country. Format and access: web maps, feature and image services with the ArcGIS REST API and a hub search API; many layers can be exported where the owner allows, and a free account adds map-making tools. Free; each layer carries its owner's licence (Creative Commons for many, Esri terms for Living Atlas). Caveats: much of the content is republished from other sources and not always current (several OpenStreetMap extracts date from 2020 to 2022), and quality and provenance vary by publisher. Simulation uses: a place to find and serve African infrastructure and hazard layers for exposure mapping, accessibility and planning models in a GIS environment. Related records: the spatial database of public health facilities in sub-Saharan Africa (data-ssa-public-health-facilities) is among the curated layers.
